# Existing Remotion composition (not generated by this skill)

Never rebuild what works. Inspect first: `package.json` (Remotion version), `src/Root.tsx` (compositions, fps, duration), the scene timeline (`Sequence from=...`), existing `<Audio>`.

## Add narration + captions

1. **Plan the segments** from the composition's scene start times (frames / fps -> seconds). Write `narration.json`:
   ```json
   { "voice": "fr_FR-upmc-medium", "speaker": 1, "speed": 1.05, "pause": 0.3, "duration": 35, "auto_shift": true,
     "segments": [ { "id": "01-intro", "start": 0.2, "text": "..." }, { "id": "02-offre", "start": 7.5, "text": "...", "spoken": "... [[ phon ]] ..." } ] }
   ```
2. **Generate** with the shared Piper environment (ask before `cv voice setup --yes` if missing):
   ```
   <piper-python> ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/voice/generate-voiceover.py --script narration.json \
     --out public/audio/voiceover --full-track voiceover-full.wav \
     --copy-manifest src/cv/voiceover.manifest.json --srt out/<name>.fr.srt
   ```
   `<piper-python>`: the path printed by `cv doctor` (usually `~/.celeste-video/venv/Scripts/python.exe`). Run from the project folder. Check `--phonemes` first for new text. Read the console: any `moved from ... to ...` means two segments collided (shorten text), any `ends after the timeline` is an overrun to fix.
3. **Wire it:** `cv attach-voice` copies `cvVoice.ts`, `CvVoiceover.tsx`, `CvSubtitles.tsx` to `src/cv/` (set `FPS` in `cvVoice.ts`; add `"resolveJsonModule": true` to tsconfig). Then in the composition:
   ```tsx
   <CvVoiceover />
   <CvSubtitles bottom={250} fontFamily={yourFont} />
   <Audio src={music} volume={(f) => musicVolume(f, 0.6, 0.2)} />   // duck the existing music
   ```
   Keep the existing music, only lower it under the voice (8 frames attack, 16 release).
4. **Review**: render stills at several frames and check captions against the logo and key UI. Render with the same memory rules as `render-memory.md`: check free RAM first (`cv doctor`), use `--concurrency=1` when memory is tight, and finish with ffprobe (codec, resolution, duration, audio stream) before saying the export succeeded. `cv render` itself only drives skill-shaped projects (storyboard + engine); for others run `npx remotion render <entry> <composition> out/x.mp4 --codec=h264 --audio-codec=aac --concurrency=1` yourself and verify the file.

## Modify an existing video (transitions, rhythm)

Change only what was asked, in small commits-like steps; keep the old output file. Typical moves: shorten holds (`durationInFrames`), tighten `interpolate` ranges, replace hard cuts by `fade`/`wipe` overlaps (start the next `Sequence` earlier and cover the previous), add anticipation (ease-in) and overshoot (`spring` damping 12-16) on key text, align hits to the music beat (beat = 60/bpm s), keep headline <= 8 words. Re-check the timeline sums and narration placement after retiming; regenerate the voice stage only if its text changed.

If the video was made by this skill, edit `video/storyboard.json` instead (Workflow D).
